summary: Implementation for Steps 10–12 (self-healing: legacy field repair + forward-compatibility) was already present in project-lifecycle.ts. Written 15 new tests covering all 6 acceptance criteria: 5 unit tests for computeHealedStatus legacySynthesisTimestampRepair flag logic; 2 integration tests for AC1+AC2 (synthesis_generated_at backfilled to last_updated + warning comment emitted); 2 integration tests for AC3 (silent ledger_version backfill to SPEC_VERSION, no comment); 3 integration tests for AC4 (forward-compat warning fires when ledger_version > SPEC_VERSION, not for equal or lower); 1 integration test for AC5 (both repairs applied in single atomic read); 2 integration tests for AC6 (no duplicate comments on repeated reads for both repair types). All 82 project-lifecycle tests pass. Full suite: 1324/1324 tests pass.

comments.note: The synthesisTimestampRepairedFlag in getProjectStatus() is set after the main withLock block and then triggers a second withLock for emitting the repair comment. A third withLock follows for ordering warnings. These three sequential locks per getProjectStatus() call when healing is needed could be collapsed into one or two for efficiency — though correctness is not affected. See project-lifecycle.ts lines ~360–420.

The forward-compat deduplication check (needsForwardCompatWarning) is evaluated on the pre-lock rootIndex snapshot but re-checked via freshNeedsForwardCompatWarning inside the lock — this is correct TOCTOU discipline. However the pattern is slightly inconsistent with how legacySynthesisTimestampRepair deduplication works (no pre-lock snapshot check for it). Both are functionally correct but the asymmetry adds cognitive load when reading the code.

summary: WP-007 code review PASS. Implementation is architecturally sound and all 6 acceptance criteria are satisfied by correct, well-tested code. computeHealedStatus() is a properly isolated pure function whose legacySynthesisTimestampRepair logic is exact: fires only when synthesis_generated=true, corruptionDetected=false, and synthesis_generated_at is null/undefined. The ledger_version semver comparison uses numeric destructuring with defaults — correct for all well-formed semver inputs. TOCTOU discipline is maintained: re-read under lock before any write, forwardCompatWarningNote deduplication checked inside the lock via freshNeedsForwardCompatWarning. The 15 new tests are well-structured (unit tests for the pure function, integration tests per AC) and the test-fixture helpers are clean and minimal. No blocking issues found.

comments.note: Three sequential withLock acquisitions in getProjectStatus() when self-healing fires (lock 1: field repair + forward-compat comment; lock 2: pipeline ordering warnings; lock 3: synthesis_generated_at repair comment). Already flagged by Developer and QA. Correctness is not affected; collapsing into fewer locks would reduce contention on high-throughput readers.

Reliability gap: synthesis_generated_at repair comment (lock 3) is emitted in a separate withLock after the field has already been persisted (lock 1). If the process exits between those two locks, the comment is permanently lost — on the next read, legacySynthesisTimestampRepair evaluates to false (timestamp is already set) so the comment-emit path is never re-entered. The field repair itself is safe; only the advisory comment is at risk. Low severity since comments are diagnostic, not functional. Mitigation: move comment push into lock 1 alongside the field write.

Version comparison uses Number() on split semver segments. If ledger_version contains a non-numeric pre-release segment (e.g. '2.5.0-beta'), Number('0-beta') yields NaN, and all comparisons (NaN > n) return false — the version would silently be treated as not-newer. Low-risk given schema validation should prevent malformed versions, but an explicit isFinite() guard in the comparison would make the intent clearer.

No code issues — implementation is clean, well-structured, and consistent with existing conventions in project-lifecycle.ts. The new tests follow established fixture patterns (createTempStore/cleanupTempStore) and the describe-block grouping per AC is a model for future self-healing test additions.
